lessons.title: What's a Turnaround?
lessons.summary: One character, seen from every side.

steps.title: Same character, every side
steps.text: A turnaround is a set of drawings of one character from different sides: front, three-quarter, side and back. Animators use it so the character looks the same in every scene, from every angle.

steps.title: Line it all up
steps.text: Draw the views side by side and run straight lines across: the top of the head, the eyes, the chin and the feet. Every view must touch the same lines, so the character never grows or shrinks.

quiz.question: Why run lines across a turnaround?
choices: So every view is the same height
quiz.explain: Matching heights keeps the character the same size from every side.

steps.title: Front and side
steps.text: Start with the front view. Then draw the side view using the same guide lines, so the eyes, chin and feet sit at the same heights. In the side view the nose sticks out past the head, and you only see one eye.

steps.title: Front view
steps.text: Trace the front view: head, eyes, nose, ears, body and feet.
steps.hint: Biggest shapes first: head and body. Then the small parts.

steps.title: Side view
steps.text: Trace the side view. Check the eye sits on the same line as before.
steps.hint: The nose pokes out past the circle of the head.

quiz.question: In a side view, how many eyes can you usually see?
quiz.explain: The other eye is hidden around the far side of the head.

steps.title: Halfway round
steps.text: The three-quarter view is halfway between front and side. The face slides toward one side: the center line (the dashed line) curves around the head, the far eye looks thinner, and the far ear hides.

steps.title: 3/4 view
steps.text: Trace the three-quarter view. Notice the far eye is narrower.
steps.hint: Use the dashed center line to place the nose.

quiz.question: In a 3/4 view, the far eye looks...
quiz.explain: It's turning away from you around the ball of the head.

steps.title: Back view
steps.text: The back view has the same outline as the front, but no face. Check that it touches the same guide lines as the other views.

steps.title: Draw the turnaround
steps.text: Draw all four views, one per frame: front, 3/4, side and back.
steps.hint: Keep the head on the top line and the feet on the bottom line every time.

quiz.question: The back view's outline matches...
choices: The front view, without a face
quiz.explain: From behind, the head and body have the same outline as from the front.
